To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the droplet spreading on homogeneous surfaces obeys a power law and that droplet spreading on heterogeneous surfaces is highly anisotropic.

we have developed a three-dimensional lattice-Boltzmann model to simulate the spreading of mesoscopic droplets on heterogeneous surfaces, and we have shown that the time evolution of the base radius of a droplet on a homogeneous substrate is a function of the dimensionless time, and the wetting velocity of a droplet spreading on a surface comprising of hydrophobic and hydropilic stripes is anisotropic.

we use a three-dimensional Lattice Boltzamnn model to investigate the droplet spreading on homogeneous and heterogeneous substrates and we found that on a homogeneous substrate the radius of the droplets grows with time as a function of viscosity and surface tension and on a heterogeneous substrate the wetting velocity and equilibrium shape of the drop is anisotropic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a lattice Boltzmann method for the simulation of droplet spreading on heterogeneous surfaces.
developing a fundamental understanding of the physics and chemistry of wetting phenomena.
the development of new computational methods for simulating the dynamics of fluids at the nanoscale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the droplet spreading on the surface with stripes of alternating hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity is not a simple process, but it is a complicated one.
the Lattice Boltzamn model is a good model for the simulation of droplets.
the droplet spreading is governed by the interplay of surface tension, viscosity and the surface energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spreading of droplet on homogeneous surfaces is a self-similar process and on a heterogeneous substrate, the spreading is a self-affine process.
the spreading dynamics of a droplet on a heterogeneous surface can be predicted from the spreading dynamics on a homogeneous surface and the equilibrium shape.
the spreading of the droplets is governed by a competition between the surface tension, viscosity and the wetting properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LBM is a powerful tool to investigate the dynamics of spreading droplets on surfaces of arbitrary complexity.
a three-dimensional model is essential for understanding the spreading of droplets on heterogeneous surfaces.
lattice Boltzmann models are well suited to simulate the spreading of droplets on heterogeneous surfaces and that the spreading of droplet is sensitive to the underlying substrate.
